projects.title: ANT Meta Bots – ML-Powered Options Trading Platform
projects.description: An end-to-end algorithmic trading platform that generates ML-based signals and autonomously executes and manages options trades in real time.
highlights: Built Lorentzian k-NN based ML system for generating LONG/SHORT signals from futures data
Automated options execution with dynamic ATM strike selection and Delta Exchange API integration
Designed unified async engine handling signal processing and trade lifecycle at 1-second intervals
Implemented full trade management: TP, SL, trailing stops, re-entry, and session-based force-close
Handled full trade lifecycle across signal → execution → monitoring → exit with strict state control and zero double-execution guarantees

architecture: End-to-end pipeline from futures data → ML signal generation → options execution
Dual live data feeds for futures (signal) and options (execution monitoring)
Multi-bot architecture supporting independent strategy instances
Session-based lifecycle management with controlled trade isolation
engineering: Unified async Watchdog engine replacing multi-component architecture
Fill verification pipeline with fallback and emergency handling
Persistent state using SQLite with automatic recovery
React dashboard with WebSocket-based real-time monitoring and control

insights.problem: Maintaining independence between multiple real-time system layers while still enabling meaningful interaction between them.
insights.why_it_was_hard: Each subsystem (data manager, live feed, signal generator, trade monitor) had its own lifecycle, data format, and execution model, making synchronization and communication extremely complex.
failure_points: Duplicate trade execution under rapid signal changes
insights.real_world_behavior: System handled multiple bots, each consuming live futures and options data independently, while executing trades in real time without double execution or state corruption.
insights.what_i_learned: True system reliability comes from controlling state transitions, not just generating better signals.

metrics.scale: Supports multiple bots, live feeds, and signal streams concurrently
metrics.latency: 1-second execution cycle across all core systems
metrics.throughput: Continuous async processing of signals, trades, and live feeds
metrics.impact: Fully automated end-to-end trading lifecycle with zero manual intervention

personality.approach: Break complex systems into independent agents with controlled interaction
personality.strength: Handling concurrency and state across multiple live components
personality.edge: Thinking in system behavior rather than isolated features

projects.title: Real-Time Trading Signal Distribution Infrastructure
projects.description: A production-grade trading execution system built for automated signal broadcasting and account-level execution.
highlights: High-performance Java server parsing multi-target trading signals from Telegram groups
Per-user distribution logic with signal deduplication and MetaTrader ID verification
Execution layer using MetaTrader EA with automated order placement and trailing stop-loss

architecture: High-performance Java server parsing multi-target trading signals from Telegram groups
Per-user distribution logic with signal deduplication and MetaTrader ID verification
Controlled broadcast routing to individual users
Execution layer using MetaTrader EA with automated order placement
Trailing stop-loss and risk management enforcement
Structured signal formatting for Telegram channels
engineering: Admin-only Telegram bot for client provisioning
Access control and backup management
Persistent state storage with self-healing recovery
Transition from trading bots to distributed trading infrastructure

insights.problem: Building a reliable system to parse, validate, and distribute trading signals from unstructured Telegram messages.
insights.why_it_was_hard: Telegram messages are inconsistent and noisy, requiring robust parsing and strict validation before execution.
tradeoffs: Flexible parsing vs strict signal structure
failure_points: Incorrect signal parsing due to format variation
insights.real_world_behavior: System continuously listens to Telegram channels, auto-reconnects on failure, and routes validated signals to individual users based on access control.
insights.what_i_learned: External APIs are unreliable by default — systems must be built assuming failure at any time.

metrics.scale: Handles multiple users and signal streams concurrently
metrics.latency: Near real-time message processing and distribution
metrics.impact: Enabled automated trading execution from live Telegram signals

projects.title: QubiForge – Multi-Layer Trading Strategy Data Pipeline
projects.description: A large-scale data pipeline for generating and analyzing trading strategies using machine learning on time-series data.
highlights: Built multi-stage pipeline to convert raw trading data into ML-ready datasets
Optimized processing time from 8–9 hours to ~10 minutes
Processed ~57 crore rows using parallel computation
Designed configurable system for large-scale strategy experimentation

architecture: Bronze Layer: SL/TP grid simulation generating millions of trade outcome combinations
Silver Layer: 200+ technical indicators + advanced support/resistance modeling
Gold Layer: Rolling-window feature normalization with price-relative scaling
Platinum Layer: Decision Tree rule mining to XGBoost model experimentation
Diamond Layer: Strategy evaluation engine (Profit Factor, Max Drawdown, cost modeling)
engineering: Optimized pipeline from 8-9 hours to ~10 minutes
Parallelized processing across large datasets (~57 crore rows)
Fully configurable via a single centralized configuration file
Designed for large-scale model training under constrained infrastructure

insights.problem: Processing massive trading datasets efficiently for ML experimentation under hardware constraints.
insights.why_it_was_hard: Traditional CSV-based workflows failed at scale due to memory and performance limitations.
failure_points: Slow I/O bottlenecks with CSV files
insights.real_world_behavior: System processes tens of crores of rows using sharded parquet files and parallel pipelines without loading full datasets into memory.
insights.what_i_learned: Data architecture decisions matter more than model selection at scale.

metrics.latency: Reduced pipeline time from 8–10 hours to under 10 minutes
metrics.impact: Enabled large-scale ML experimentation on limited hardware

personality.approach: Fix bottlenecks at data architecture level, not just code level

projects.title: Elastic DCA – Real-Time Trading Automation System
projects.description: A re-architected fullstack trading system with a decoupled execution engine, enabling deterministic trade management, real-time control, and advanced risk handling.
highlights: Rebuilt system with decoupled backend engine and MQL5 execution layer for reliability
WebSocket-based real-time communication between backend and trading dashboard
Advanced risk controls including loss limits, hedge triggers, and basket-level TP/SL
Dynamic preset management system with database-backed configuration

architecture: Decoupled FastAPI backend handling trading logic independent of MT5
Step-based execution pipeline for deterministic trade lifecycle management
Independent grid systems for buy/sell with full isolation
Modular services enabling scalable system extension
engineering: Database-backed state replacing file-based persistence
Tick queue processing with staleness checks for real-time consistency
Bulk action dispatching to EA for optimized execution
Environment-driven configuration for flexible deployment

insights.problem: Keeping backend server state perfectly synchronized with MetaTrader execution in real time.
insights.why_it_was_hard: Server and trading terminal operate independently, leading to inconsistencies in trade state and PnL calculations.
failure_points: PnL mismatches between server and MT5
insights.real_world_behavior: Server processes live ticks, maps trades from MetaTrader, and controls execution decisions in real time.
insights.what_i_learned: Synchronization requires shared standards, not direct control.

metrics.scale: Handles multiple grid systems and trade flows

personality.approach: Design shared contracts instead of forcing direct control between systems
personality.strength: Solving synchronization problems across independent runtimes

architecture: Custom 3D cube state representation engine
CFOP algorithm implementation (Cross, F2L, OLL, PLL)

Polymorphism-driven modular architecture
engineering: CLI visualization with color-coded output

Shift from interface-building to computational system design

insights.problem: Simulating and solving a Rubik’s Cube computationally using real-world solving methods.
insights.why_it_was_hard: Representing a 3D cube structure and implementing CFOP logic programmatically required deep algorithmic understanding.
failure_points: Inefficient state transitions in early design
insights.real_world_behavior: Engine generates thousands of CFOP-based solutions and selects the most optimal one in real time.
insights.what_i_learned: Breaking down complex systems into smaller deterministic steps makes them solvable.

personality.approach: Model real-world systems mathematically and solve via iteration
personality.strength: Breaking complex logic into deterministic steps
personality.edge: Persistence on long-term problem solving (7 months build)
